why: Image 1 keeps deep blacks and a saturated, believable tinted-acrylic red, so the speakers read as solid objects sitting in a dim, lamp-lit room. Image 2's glass reflections are a nice through-the-window cue, but the haze lies evenly over the whole frame: it flattens contrast, turns the cabinets a chalky glowing pink and lifts the plinth, so the picture reads as an overlay rather than real glass.
